sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The global filter has a query mode: tick the new Q box beside Cc, Rx and Ex, and the box reads the query language majkinetor's Event Horizon uses (credited). "format:cd" keeps the rows whose Format column contains "cd" (the start of a column name will do: "form:cd"), "-live" and "-(live OR demo)" leave rows out, OR and AND (in capitals) combine terms, quotes keep a phrase or a space together, and a Date or Year column takes ranges such as "date:1990-1995", "2016-" or "-1987". Side by side means AND, so "type:album year:1975-1985 -live" is the albums of those years that are not live; a lower-case "rock and roll" stays one phrase. A card under the field says what the query means as you type, what is still missing ("Format: type a value") and when a key names no column, and its Syntax button lists the rules. Ex turns the whole query round, Cc applies to every term, Q and Rx switch each other off, only the matching terms are highlighted, each sub-table uses its own columns, and a pinned or recent filter remembers its Q. Off on every new page; with Q off nothing changes, and plain filtering is as fast as before. A query searches every row on each key (a query can widen as you type), so on a very large table it is a little slower than a plain word.
